doc: The STANDARD project-report parts, declared with the same fields a store extension's reporting.json uses (src/extensions/reporting-v1.mjs), so the composition rules treat both alike. The network collectors run in Node (the credential never leaves that process); every other part is Python, run through python/orbit_part.py.

parts.doc: Pull requests, reviews, issues, Projects v2 items, Actions runs and deployments from GitHub or GitHub Enterprise Server, one batch per run with full pagination
Boards work items (as of the cut-off), Repos pull requests and Pipelines builds and deployments from Azure DevOps Services or Server, one batch per run with full pagination
Planning documents in a BMAD-style tree (stories with Status lines, epics, PRD requirements), read as they were at the last commit before the cut-off
The standard model every standard section draws, and the headline KPIs

metrics.label: Pull requests merged
metrics.definition: Pull requests merged inside the window, whenever they were opened.

metrics.label: Merges per week
metrics.definition: Pull requests merged inside the window divided by the window's length in weeks. A proxy for delivery pace, not a deployment frequency.

metrics.label: Median cycle time
metrics.definition: Median elapsed calendar hours from a pull request being opened to being merged, over PRs merged in the window.

metrics.label: Cycle time, 85th percentile
metrics.definition: 85th percentile of open-to-merge hours over PRs merged in the window.

metrics.label: Median lead time (PR proxy)
metrics.definition: Median hours from a PR's first commit (committer date) to its merge. A PR-based proxy, not the DORA lead time for changes.

metrics.label: Median pickup time
metrics.definition: Median hours from a PR being ready for review to its first human review submitted before the merge.

metrics.label: Median PR size
metrics.definition: Median of lines added plus deleted over PRs merged in the window. Generated files and lockfiles are included. Unknown -- never zero -- when the source does not report lines changed (Azure Repos).

metrics.label: XL pull requests
metrics.definition: Share of PRs merged in the window with more than 1,000 lines changed, over the PRs whose size the source reports.

metrics.label: Human review before merge
metrics.definition: Share of PRs merged in the window with at least one review from a person other than the author, submitted before the merge. Bot reviews never count.

metrics.label: Approved before merge
metrics.definition: Share of PRs merged in the window with an approval submitted before the merge.

metrics.label: Merged with threads unresolved at capture
metrics.definition: Share of PRs merged in the window that had a review thread unresolved WHEN THE DATA WAS COLLECTED. The source keeps no history of resolution, so this is not the state at merge.

metrics.label: Fix share (proxy)
metrics.definition: Share of PRs merged in the window classified as fixes from their title or branch. A proxy for repair load, not a change-failure rate.

metrics.label: AI-authored commits (floor)
metrics.definition: Share of commits in PRs merged in the window whose author, committer or trailer carries a configured AI marker. AI work committed under a person's name is invisible, so this is a floor.

metrics.label: Open pull requests at cut-off
metrics.definition: Pull requests opened before the cut-off and neither merged nor closed at it.

metrics.label: Work items completed
metrics.definition: Work items whose last move into a Completed-category state falls in the window and that were still completed at the cut-off. One item linked to several PRs is one item.

metrics.label: Work items completed per week
metrics.definition: Work items completed in the window divided by its length in weeks.

metrics.label: Median work item cycle time
metrics.definition: Median hours from a work item's first move into an In Progress-category state to its completion, over items completed in the window.

metrics.label: Backlog at cut-off
metrics.definition: Work items in a Proposed, In Progress or Resolved category at the cut-off. Canceled (Removed) items are excluded; states the source gives no category are listed separately.

metrics.label: Successful deployments per week
metrics.definition: Successful deployment records in the window divided by its length in weeks. Only when the source records deployments.

metrics.label: Build success
metrics.definition: Share of finished builds in the window that succeeded, over those that succeeded, failed or partially succeeded.

parts.doc: A throughput Monte Carlo over the complete periods of this window, or no forecast and the reason

sections.title: Contributors
sections.note: Per-person numbers. Off by default: counts of pull requests, lines and comments are activity, never productivity.
